title: Titanium Underwater Camera Housing
alloyReason: Grade 23 Ti-6Al-4V ELI (UNS R56401) is mandated for Titanium Underwater Camera Housing where extra-low interstitial elements (O ≤0.13%, Fe ≤0.25%) provide superior fracture toughness (KIC >100 MPa√m) and fatigue crack growth resistance compared to standard Grade 5. The controlled oxygen content reduces susceptibility to strain-rate embrittlement, making it the preferred choice for Deep-sea camera/sensor pressure housing in safety-critical applications. This rationale is driven by deep-sea camera/sensor pressure housing and fat life requirements.

inspection: UT wall thickness scan (deepsea camerasensor verified)

faq.q: How does Titanium Underwater Camera Housing perform in deep-sea pressure environments?
faq.a: Titanium Underwater Camera Housing fabricated from Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V is suitable for full-ocean-depth operation (11,000 m, 110 MPa external pressure). With 830 MPa yield strength and spherical/cylindrical collapse pressure margins >2× for deepsea camerasensor pressure, titanium's strength-to-weight ratio provides the deepest diving capability per unit mass of any structural metal. Buckling analysis per API 1111 is provided for each design.

faq.q: What material certifications are provided with Titanium Underwater Camera Housing?
faq.a: Each Titanium Underwater Camera Housing shipment includes EN 10204 Type 3.1 mill test certificate with chemical analysis, mechanical properties, and heat identification. Dimensional inspection reports and Certificate of Conformance (CoC) are standard. First Article Inspection Reports (FAIR) per AS9102 are available on request for deepsea camerasensor pressure.
